flows.description: Reject non-synthetic repository inputs, formatting errors, lint violations and invalid types.
Validate the existing isolated synthetic development stack configuration.
Run strict CPU workloads without competing native flows, then reject substituted source, incomplete cases and unsafe cleanup.

runtime.launch: A one-worker Vitest preflight executes the strict files before the Python ownership and accounting cases. Every other native flow waits for this gate. A same-source, same-attempt, same-coordinator proof binds its complete report for one main-phase consumer.
runtime.health: Preflight and main Vitest partitions must form the complete reviewed unit inventory exactly once. Existing five-second deadlines, all 1,440 minute attempts, real hashes, JSON CAS accounting and Python failure controls remain.
runtime.cleanup: Owned leases prevent report replacement. Main claims the preflight proof once; missing, stale, mismatched or overlapping results fail. Existing temporary checkout and process cleanup remains mandatory.

flows.description: Build the daily-refreshed isolated PDF reader, adversarial probe and malware scanner images on the provisioned rootless daemon.

runtime.launch: The native command builds immutable reader, probe and scanner targets on the provisioned rootless socket, retaining the daily security-package and malware-signature refresh.
runtime.health: Rootless engine policy, immutable image digests and a clean synthetic scanner preflight must pass before owner-only runtime configurations are atomically replaced.
runtime.cleanup: The builder removes its bounded temporary iid files; the immutable images and owner-only digest configurations remain for dependent verification flows.

flows.description: Replay all migrations and verify canonical synthetic scenario invariants in owned local D1.

runtime.launch: The native seed runner resets the default synthetic scenario and replays every migration. After the base synthetic seed closes, it exports an isolated browser copy before applying default-only additions and checking all canonical invariants. It then verifies the browser binding/readback and seals all source inputs and persisted bytes.
runtime.health: Scenario readback assertions check migrations, seeds and relationships.
runtime.cleanup: Wrangler exits; disposable synthetic state remains under ignored .keel-local.

flows.description: Execute the complementary native domain, API, database, client, workflow, resource and billing cases, then validate the complete preflight/main unit union.

runtime.launch: After the isolated gate, Vitest runs every remaining unit case with three workers. The native command first claims the exact-source and same-attempt preflight proof, then verifies the complementary report and complete union. The unchanged first-ready map order controls admission; each real D1 cost fixture copies a verified closed seed into its own fresh runtime. Unit PDF configuration remains explicitly absent.
runtime.health: Repository/API readbacks, real D1 billing metadata and SQL query plans validate behavior. Populated OLD-schema cases meter actual D1 rows before pending SQL and certify preservation. Capacity cases exercise conditional R2, cumulative quotas, expiry and denied work.
runtime.cleanup: Native teardown disposes workerd and temporary files; the helper rejects lingering owned descendants.

flows.description: Prove real Chromium popup capture through production tsx, scanning and PDF extraction without an unrelated application server.

runtime.launch: The existing isolated Chromium fixture runs as a real tsx child with its unchanged 50-second deadline and 128 KiB output cap. Production collector defaults retain the real scanner and reader.
runtime.health: Zod validates the complete capture; exact request/download counts, one capture/document and the original legal-name/page assertions must pass.
runtime.cleanup: The child closes Chromium in finally; the native owner enforces the outer deadline and descendant cleanup. This flow completes before either the four-worker UI suite or the remaining PDF probes start.

flows.description: Validate the sealed isolated D1 fixture produced by the canonical migration gate.

runtime.launch: The native command exclusively acquires the Playwright lease and validates the closed browser fixture already produced by the successful canonical migration gate. It performs no duplicate reset or migration pass.
runtime.health: A source-input digest and complete prepared-tree digest seal the verified fixture; the browser consumer rejects missing, stale, mutated or symlinked state without rebuilding it.
runtime.cleanup: Failure leaves no valid seal. The prepared browser command consumes the exact owned seed after cloning, while a later preparation safely replaces an unconsumed owned seed.

flows.description: Build every workspace and enforce the native 100 KiB initial JavaScript gzip budget and lazy application boundary.
Exercise the complete desktop/mobile browser contract, including minimal review, automatic decisions, persisted saves, layout, recovery and real synthetic document capture.

runtime.launch: The sealed, verified and closed synthetic D1 fixture is copied into three independent profiles without rerunning setup. Three one-worker stateful shards and the one-worker production-served API-mocked lane start on distinct ports; only after all four validate and release their runtimes does the four-worker production-served holdings lane start.
runtime.health: The development stateful lane validates the initial Vite module graph; all stateful lanes also wait through the web proxy for /api/holdings-page. Mocked contexts reject unhandled application APIs. Five validated reports must cover the complete reviewed browser inventory with unchanged snapshots and at most four active browser workers.
runtime.cleanup: Owned lane process groups are terminated on completion, failure or cancellation before profile removal. Per-suite leases prevent duplicate report and runtime writers.

flows.description: Run real synthetic reader, scanner and adversarial isolation probes, including resource exhaustion and owned-container removal.

runtime.launch: Source checks complete before scanner isolation starts. The verifier shares one cross-process capacity owner per daemon across its scanner/reader and kernel-probe sequences, with unchanged container limits and explicit caller-death/contending-reader proof.
runtime.health: Inspect plus kernel handshake and synthetic reader/scanner probes establish the runtime policy.
runtime.cleanup: The independent owner removes its exact container and proves absence before releasing capacity; caller death cannot bypass cleanup. Dirty ownership refuses admission; no shared daemon or image cleanup.

requirements.description: All reviewed native cases and runner variants must execute with accepted outcomes; omitted, skipped, replaced or filtered cases fail.
Keep repository inputs synthetic, D1 canonical, financial arithmetic integer and accepted decisions/forecasts append-only.
Routine observations use recorded deterministic acceptance; identity, evidence and planning exceptions retain explicit decisions and minimal valid submission.
Use the accepted shared compositions and responsive controls, keep primary actions clear, preserve invalid drafts and saved-state behavior.
Keep GETs projection-only with fixed round trips and independent D1 billing/query-plan ceilings across positive, empty, 120-item, historical and unrelated-household cases.
Preserve combined idle, outage and useful-work budgets, bounded queue admission, unchanged replay, latency, cancellation and current authorization.
Validate external inputs and authenticate fail-closed, preserving evidence before accepted state.

Preserve reader/scanner isolation, input/output/time limits, bounded document capture/cache and backup count/bytes, integrity and exact owned cleanup. Enforce bounded GitHub bundles, retention and aggregate artifact admission without deleting backups or foreign evidence.
Exercise success, failure and cancellation cleanup and explicit retained-run ownership; external seven-day collector activation remains outside this pilot.
Preserve locked bootstrap, synthetic migrations, focused commands, build validity and the existing initial JavaScript budget.
Preserve accepted source pins, merge verification, secret scan, protected deployment ordering, exact release evidence and production approval.
